headline: With the dynamic value on an inline style and no class to generate, the only cost left is the wrapper each build keeps: folding takes `next-yak-9.7` to `vanilla` (0.642 against 0.603 ms/1k), turning it off costs 40%, and the 9.6.0 runtime costs 2.2×.

microbench.why: The control case generates no class for the dynamic value at all, so it measures the styling wrapper and nothing else. Folded, `next-yak-9.7` renders at 0.642 ms/1k against `vanilla`'s 0.603 with a 0.230 ms library slice. Switching folding off restores the `Yak` component and costs 40% (0.900 ms/1k, library slice 0.496), and the 9.6.0 runtime costs 2.2× (1.32 ms/1k, 0.677 ms). This is folding's cleanest measurement in the study.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` serves 1189 req/s and the folded lane 1178, a tie. Without folding the wrapper costs 25% (892 req/s) and the 9.6.0 runtime 47% (624). The gap tracks the library slice exactly.

attribution.why: `next-yak-9.7` renders in 0.749 ms and `vanilla` in 0.768, the folded build slightly ahead because its class name is shorter than the hand-written one. Folding off costs 0.337 ms of extra render, essentially all library slice (0.496 against 0.230 ms), and the 9.6.0 runtime 0.653 ms. Nothing here is styling work; it is one React component per element or none.

hydrate.why: Hydration is pure JS in all four builds, 50.8-58.5 ms with no style or layout in the span. The folded build and `vanilla` are indistinguishable at 50.8 and 51.6 ms. The wrapper costs a little client work too, 54.1 ms without folding and 58.5 for 9.6.0.

inp.why: Moving one dot costs 0.44-0.70 ms of JS and 7.1-7.6 ms of frame in every build. A single re-render is too small for the wrapper to matter, so the four lanes tie.

mount.why: Cold mount puts the folded build at `vanilla`'s level, 68.3 against 68.1 ms. The unfolded wrapper costs 3.2 ms over the folded build and the 9.6.0 runtime 7.4, the same ordering the SSR profile shows, scaled down by the browser's fixed sheet-parse and paint cost.

renderTiming.why: One recalculation and one layout in all four builds, the recalc at 0.123-0.146 ms. There is one static rule on the page whatever the wrapper does.

payload.why: `vanilla` ships 5.50 kB gzipped and the folded build 6.53, the difference being next-yak's runtime module, which folding shrinks but does not remove from the bundle. Folding off adds 232 B and the 9.6.0 build 21 B on top of the folded one. Payload is the one axis where folding barely helps.

nsweep.why: At 4000 dots the folded build holds 2.82 ms against `vanilla`'s 2.68, both linear in n with one rule. Without folding the per-element wrapper multiplies by n and reaches 3.87 ms, and the 9.6.0 runtime 6.00. The wrapper is a per-instance cost, so the sweep magnifies it.

crossCase: `dyn-inline` closes the dynamic trio (the Examples `dyn-translate` and `dyn-fair` above). It carries only the next-yak family and `vanilla` because it is the reference floor for a value that never needs a class: with no styling work left to hide behind, the numbers are the wrapper. Folded, `next-yak-9.7` ties `vanilla` at 0.642 against 0.603 ms/1k, which is also why its figures in `dyn-translate` and `dyn-fair` are the same as each other, the compiler having already produced this shape.
